steps.title: Define the EventMap type interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface called EventMap that uses a generic type parameter to define event names as keys and their payload types as values.
steps.hint: Use the TypeScript interface syntax with a generic type parameter. The keys should be strings and the values should be any type.
steps.expectedOutcome: An EventMap interface that can be used to type event names and their payloads throughout the emitter implementation.
successCriteria: EventMap interface is defined with a generic type parameter and uses index signature syntax to map string keys to values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the EventMap interface. This will serve as the foundation for typing our event emitter.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your interface uses the correct syntax with a generic type parameter and properly maps string keys to values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The EventMap interface needs to be defined with a generic type parameter. Try using: interface EventMap<T> { [key: string]: T; }

steps.title: Create the TypedEventEmitter class
steps.instruction: Create a class named TypedEventEmitter that accepts a generic type parameter T extending EventMap.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword followed by the class name and generic type parameter. The generic should extend your EventMap interface.

// Create your EventMap interface here

steps.expectedOutcome: A class definition with a generic type parameter that extends EventMap.
successCriteria: The TypedEventEmitter class is defined with a generic type parameter T extending EventMap.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TypedEventEmitter class with the correct generic type constraint.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the class has a generic type parameter that extends EventMap.
steps.feedbackWrong: The class definition is missing or incorrect. Ensure you create a class named TypedEventEmitter with a generic type parameter extending EventMap.

steps.title: Initialize the listeners storage
steps.instruction: Inside the TypedEventEmitter class, add a private property named 'listeners' that stores event listeners. Use the EventMap type to ensure it's properly typed: it should be a map where each event key points to an array of callback functions.
steps.hint: The property should be private and typed as Record<K, Array<callback>> where K extends keyof EventMap. Initialize it as an empty object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TypedEventEmitter class will have a private 'listeners' property that is properly typed to store arrays of callback functions for each event.
successCriteria: The class contains a private property named 'listeners' typed as Record<K, Array<(payload: EventMap[K]) => void>> where K extends keyof EventMap, initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the private listeners property with proper typing. This storage will hold all event callbacks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a listeners property, but check: is it private? Is it properly typed using EventMap? Did you initialize it as an empty object?
steps.feedbackWrong: The listeners property is missing or incorrect. It should be a private property that stores arrays of callback functions, typed with EventMap.

steps.title: Implement the on method
steps.instruction: Add an 'on' method to your TypedEventEmitter class that accepts an event name (typed as keyof EventMap) and a callback function (typed to match the event's payload), then stores the callback in the listeners map.
steps.hint: The method signature should be: on<K extends keyof EventMap>(event: K, callback: (payload: EventMap[K]) => void): void. Inside the method, push the callback into the listeners array for that event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TypedEventEmitter class will have a properly typed 'on' method that can register event listeners with type safety.
successCriteria: The 'on' method is added to the class with correct TypeScript generics, accepts event name and callback parameters, and stores the callback in the listeners map.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the type-safe 'on' method. The method signature ensures the callback receives the correct payload type for each event.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an 'on' method, but check: 1) Does it use generics to type the event parameter? 2) Does the callback parameter match the event's payload type? 3) Does it properly store the callback in the listeners map?
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'on' method is missing or incorrect. Remember: 1) Use generics: on<K extends keyof EventMap>(event: K, ...) 2) The callback should be (payload: EventMap[K]) => void 3) Push the callback into this.listeners[event] array.

steps.title: Implement the off method
steps.instruction: Add an 'off' method to the TypedEventEmitter class that removes a specific callback from the listeners for a given event. The method should accept an event name and the callback to remove, and return void.
steps.hint: Inside the class, define a method named 'off' with type parameters matching the 'on' method. Use the event name to get the listener array, then filter out the callback to remove.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TypedEventEmitter class now has an 'off' method that can remove a specific callback for a typed event.
successCriteria: The 'off' method is defined with proper TypeScript generics, accesses the listeners array, and filters out the callback to remove.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the 'off' method with type safety. This allows removing specific event listeners.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the 'off' method uses the same generic type parameters as 'on' and correctly filters the callback from the listeners array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'off' method is missing or incorrect. It should accept an event name and callback, then remove that callback from the listeners array for that event.

steps.title: Implement the emit method
steps.instruction: Add an emit method to the TypedEventEmitter class that calls all registered callbacks for a given event with the provided payload.
steps.hint: The method should accept an event name and data, retrieve the listener array for that event, and call each callback with the data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The class will have a complete emit method that can trigger events with type-checked data.
successCriteria: The emit method is added to the class, accepts an event name and payload, and calls all registered callbacks for that event.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The emit method is now implemented and will properly trigger events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check that it correctly retrieves the listener array and calls each callback with the data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The emit method is missing or doesn't match the expected signature. Review the method structure and type parameters.

steps.title: Create a UserEvents type definition
steps.instruction: Create a type alias named UserEvents that defines specific event names and their payload types for user-related events.
steps.hint: Use the type keyword to create a type alias. Define event names as keys and their payload types as values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A UserEvents type alias is created with at least two event definitions.
successCriteria: The UserEvents type alias is defined with proper TypeScript syntax and includes event names with their payload types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a concrete event map type for user events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to define a type alias named UserEvents with event names and their payload types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserEvents type definition is missing or incorrect. Please create a type alias with event names and their payload types.

steps.instruction: Create an instance of TypedEventEmitter using the UserEvents type as the generic parameter. Declare it as a constant named 'userEmitter'.
steps.hint: Use the 'new' keyword followed by the class name with the UserEvents generic type argument.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed event emitter instance with the UserEvents type. This gives you type-safe event handling.

steps.title: Register event listeners with type checking
steps.instruction: Use the on method to register a type-safe callback for the 'login' event on your emitter instance.
steps.hint: Call the on method on your emitter instance, passing 'login' as the event name and a callback function that receives the typed data parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The emitter instance will have a properly typed callback registered for the 'login' event.
successCriteria: The on method is called on the emitter instance with 'login' as the event name and a callback function that receives the typed data parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully registered a type-safe event listener. TypeScript will ensure the callback receives the correct data type for the 'login' event.
